title: Watch a scan and stop it
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

mid-scan-shares-never-exceed-parent: needs first: A folder rolled-up-size read path that fixes a consistent view (a store.Count high-water mark captured before the parent is read, plus a rule for in-place hardlink corrections) must exis…

Is a one-level list of the scan root's direct children enough to close PS-002's 'results fill in as it goes', or does the person expect drill-down into folders in this slice? Drill-down needs the two spike-blocked items (the store published before Finish with an ordered child-range publish, and a consistent rollup read path), so it is a later slice. This design assumes the one-level list closes C4.

Uncontested: a flat ListBox of the root's children, replaced by the tree slice's first level later, versus building the TreeView shell now. Chosen to avoid the two 'needs first' items and to stay light.
Uncontested: a pending-folder counter for Done or Reading versus deriving state from listing order. Chosen because it does not depend on the stack order the survey did not describe.
Uncontested: the tracker publishes unsorted and the view sorts, versus the tracker keeping a sorted structure.
Uncontested: no percentages or share bars at all, versus shares labelled 'so far'.
Uncontested: verifying through a counts-only --report extension versus having the hook log the final counts. Both fit the recorded window-test approach.
Uncontested: state suffix wording ('reading...', 'not read yet', 'stopped partway', 'could not be opened', 'link, not followed'). Exact text is settled at build.
